title: Distance on the Coordinate Plane Practice
description: Practice finding horizontal, vertical, and diagonal distances using coordinate differences.

questions.question: Find the distance between A(-4, 3) and B(2, 3).
questions.explanation: The y-coordinates are the same, so this is horizontal distance. Compare x-values: |2 - (-4)| = 6 units.

questions.question: Find the distance between C(5, -2) and D(5, 4).
questions.explanation: The x-coordinates are the same, so this is vertical distance. Compare y-values: |4 - (-2)| = 6 units.

questions.question: If two points have the same y-coordinate, their distance can be found by comparing the x-coordinates.
questions.explanation: Points with the same y-coordinate are horizontally aligned, so the horizontal distance is the absolute difference of the x-coordinates.

questions.question: Which formula finds the diagonal distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
questions.explanation: Diagonal distance comes from the Pythagorean Theorem, so use d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2).

questions.question: Find the distance between E(0, 0) and F(3, 4). Give the number of units.
questions.explanation: The coordinate differences are 3 and 4, so d = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(25) = 5 units.

questions.question: For points P(-2, -1) and Q(4, 7), what are the positive coordinate differences?
Explain why the distance between G(-3, 2) and H(-3, -5) is 7 units.
questions.correctAnswer: The x-coordinates are the same, so the segment is vertical. Compare the y-coordinates: |2 - (-5)| = 7, so the distance is 7 units.
questions.explanation: A correct explanation identifies the same x-coordinate and uses the absolute difference of the y-coordinates.

questions.question: Find the distance between R(-1, 2) and S(5, 10).
questions.explanation: The coordinate differences are 6 and 8. Then d = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 units.
